title: Scan three items with a handheld barcode scanner, turning the one whose code faces away, and bag them
instruction: Scan the shopping and put it in the bagging area.
context: Checkout work is one of the commonest jobs there is, and most of it is this: find the barcode on each item, point the scanner at it, hear it read once, and bag the item. The skill is physical. The scanner is a tool held by its grip whose window has to be aimed at a small target at the right distance and angle; a code that faces the wrong way has to be found and the item turned with the other hand; and each item has to be read exactly once, because an unread item in the bag is stock walking out unpaid and a second read charges the customer twice. Here three items stand on a checkout counter: a tin of beans, a carton of crackers and a juice carton. The crackers' barcode faces the robot, the juice's faces its right front, and the tin's faces away. A cordless handheld scanner stands in its cradle, a bagging tray is at one side and a customer display has one lamp per item.
setup: Counter top is z = 0.7475 m; positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left. All real size; shapes are CAD models. (1) Cordless handheld barcode scanner, free, 180 g: pistol grip 34 x 30 mm in section and 112 mm tall, head 100 mm long, 160 mm tall overall; its red scan window faces forward and 10 degrees down. It stands on the foot of its grip in (2) its charging cradle, fixed, 96 x 86 x 30 mm, socket 42 x 38 mm and 18 mm deep at (0.33, -0.36). (3) Tin of baked beans, free, 66 mm across, 110 mm tall, 300 g, at (0.375, 0.13); its barcode is 85 mm up on the side AWAY from the robot. (4) Carton of crackers, free, 110 x 55 x 170 mm, 200 g, at (0.40, -0.01); barcode on its narrow face toward the robot, 110 mm up. (5) Gable-top juice carton, free, 60 x 60 x 140 mm, 250 g, at (0.47, -0.11), standing turned 70 degrees; its barcode, 90 mm up, faces the robot's right front. Barcodes are white patches 45 x 30 mm with black bars. The goods stand on (6) a rubber counter mat, 220 x 380 x 2 mm. (7) Bagging tray, fixed, 240 x 220 mm, rim 22 mm, centre (0.36, 0.29). (8) Customer display on a pole at (0.62, 0.12), fixed, 285 mm tall, turned toward the robot's right, with three lamps captioned BEANS, CRACKERS and JUICE, unlit. Real trial: an ordinary cordless scanner paired to a laptop that logs each read with its time; dummy goods of the same size and weight (empty carton with a weight, sealed tin, water-filled juice carton) with printed barcodes; the lamps may be replaced by the laptop's screen.
scoring: Read from measured poses every step. A read of an item registers when the scanner's window is aimed at its barcode: barcode centre 5 to 20 cm from the window centre and within 3 cm of the window's axis line, axis within 30 degrees of the barcode's normal, held 0.5 s. A code is read again (a double charge) if the aim has left it for 0.5 s and then holds on it again. An item is in the tray when its whole bounding box is inside the tray's outline and it rests on the tray's floor, standing or lying; it counts as bagged once it is also let go (both grippers at least 3 cm from it). Each item earns 1/3 when it has been read exactly once and is bagged at the end. An item that is in the tray for 0.5 s without having been read latches unscanned_in_bag: that item earns nothing and the trial is capped at 0.33, even if it is read afterwards. Every extra read takes 1/3 off (floor 0); the item read twice also earns nothing. An item that leaves the counter earns nothing. With all three items earned the score is 0.9 while the scanner is in a hand, and 1.0 once it is out of the hands (standing in its cradle or lying on the counter, both grippers at least 8 cm from its grip) for 1 s. How the scanner and the item are brought together is free: an item held up to the scanner in its cradle is read by the same rule. Doing nothing scores 0. Reported: reads per item, double reads, items bagged, the flag, scanner put down. Real trial: the scanner's own log gives the reads per item and their times (a code logged twice is a double charge); the video shows whether an item went into the tray before its read; at the end the judge checks that all three stand or lie wholly inside the tray and that the scanner is out of the grippers.
reset_notes: Fixed starting poses, no randomisation; arms at the ready pose. Real trial: goods set on tape marks, the tin with its barcode turned away from the robot; scanner log cleared.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, rigid bodies. The scanner reads nothing optically: a read is a rule on the measured poses of the scanner and the items (distance, angle, aim, 0.5 s hold); things in between are ignored, so a code can be read through a gripper or another item. Lamps are visuals switched by the rule. Colliders are primitives under CAD visuals: scanner two boxes, cradle a socket of blocks 2 to 4 mm wider than drawn, cartons boxes, tin a cylinder, tray a floor and four walls. Labels are thin geometry.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 993 steps (the scanner stayed in its cradle; nothing was read or bagged); termination: task_budget_limit (the runner's cap of 20 requests per task). Scripted demo: 1 after 1,403 steps.
